CS10-01.note: Text says the binder kept reacting and 'required' seawater; A is the only option in that direction. B/C/D are coherent misreadings (crystals as decay, a protective skin, portland-style finished curing) but none survives the last sentence. passage_needed false: the Roman marine-concrete/al-tobermorite story is widely known, and A is the option any reader who recognises the topic picks without the text - this is exactly the subject-recall channel.

CS10-02.note: Shallow cores yield FEWER layers and waves rework the top couplets - removal in shallow water, not addition in deep. A inverts the site and the direction, C and D substitute a counting rule and compaction, both real limnological processes a student could believe. Direction plus location must both be read, so the option set alone does not decide it.

CS10-03.note: 'They governed how many pages a number ran, not which characters survived it' fixes C and kills A, its exact inversion. D contradicts the text outright (figures DID reach the writing desk); B imports reprinting, never mentioned. Every distractor maps to a live misreading of the last sentence.

CS10-04.note: The final sentence is the concession: experienced recruits ignore the dance. A is the trap worth having - it accurately describes the MIDDLE of the passage (the vector flown out to sea), so a student who skims the question stem picks it. B and D describe nothing in the text. Needs the passage because the item is about which sentence does what.

CS10-05.note: D is lifted verbatim from the penultimate sentence, which makes this the easiest item here. B (storing water) is the strong distractor - it is the intuitive reason to haul gravel and it is the opposite of what graded gravel does. A restates the erosion account the text is displacing; C (frost heave) corresponds to no misreading in the text and is the weak leg of the set.

CS10-06.note: Best item in the batch. The finding (clustering by hand) refutes the CRITICS' device claim, not the editors' practice, so A is wrong-direction: scribal clustering supports emendation. D is the near-miss and I considered flagging it - but the survey sorts 'by copyist rather than by passage', so passage-level frequency is precisely what it did not measure; D asserts a finding the text disclaims. Not defensible, but it is the distractor a strong student loses time on.

CS10-07.note: CONFIRMS the elimination finding on option A: it is contradicted twice over - by the text ('on windy or overcast nights the city and the countryside read within half a degree') and by the physics, since the nocturnal UHI is a radiative-cooling difference that cloud suppresses. A is rejectable with no passage at all, which forces distractor_quality to weak. B (rural station siting) is also free-floating - nothing in the text is about station placement. C is the one good distractor: it substitutes dilution across the DAY for dilution across the YEAR, a real misreading, but the text's variation is night-to-night and seasonal ('not spread evenly through the year', 'fewer than thirty nights'), so C is not defensible.

CS10-08.note: Two-slot permutation set; the last sentence states B almost verbatim ('genealogies may be inherited, but the quarrels were composed'). D is the clean inversion and the only serious rival; A and C are the remaining permutations and are mechanical rather than psychologically real, which caps the set at plausible. The option set alone cannot decide which pair goes in which slot.

CS10-09.note: 'The color curve, and not the total energy released, is what identified the debris' names D and explicitly pre-rejects B. C (nickel abundance) is the expectation that failed and A (onset delay) is a real kilonova observable never mentioned here - both are things a student who half-remembers GW170817 would reach for. Note this is the other item where subject recall could substitute for reading, but the options do not give the mechanism away on their own.

CS10-10.note: Cash deposit plus a landowning guarantor is a resource threshold, and the closing line ('destitution kept them off it') seals C. A overshoots to the top of the distribution when the text says the middle. D is the best distractor - agriculturally sensible, entirely absent from the text - and B is the weakest leg but still a plausible chain-migration story.

CS10-11.note: Text 2 states the dumbbell pupil / depth-of-focus mechanism directly, so with the passage it is easy. passage_needed FALSE: the distractors are the three OTHER famous monochromat colour hacks - layered retina, oil droplets (birds), sweeping filter - and anyone who has met the 2016 cephalopod chromatic-aberration hypothesis picks the pupil option from the option set alone. Strong distractors, but they are strong in a way that rewards recall rather than reading.

CS10-12.note: 'Sealed instruments deposited with the town council' is a third party, stated outright. C (private ledgers) and D (unwritten custom) are good misreadings of 'recorded elsewhere' and 'no occasion to repeat'; B (word of mouth) simply re-states the Text 1 reading Text 2 is rejecting and is the weak leg.

CS10-13.note: Text 2's whole argument is growth/fecundity cost cashed out on storm-scoured reefs, and Text 1's final sentence is the persistence claim A answers. C (carbon cost) is the real physiological mechanism BEHIND the slow growth and is the trap for a student who knows symbiont biology; B (reversion) and D (recovery) are plausible coral-reef costs found nowhere in Text 2. The option set names four different costs, so the passage decides which one Text 2 actually argues.

CS10-14.note: Text 2 is entirely about ignition temperature and combustion rate, so D with the passage is immediate. passage_needed FALSE: the Neanderthal manganese-dioxide-as-fire-making result is well circulated, and D is the only option that is not either the pigment reading being rebutted (B) or an invention (A heat retention, C groove cutting). A reader who knows the topic never opens Text 2.

CS10-16.note: The hard item of the pair. 'Where many substrates were mixed, the order settles on the pattern Text 1 describes ... it surfaces where the inherited options conflict' - the bioprogram holds where substrates DISAGREED. B is the exact inversion and is the answer a student gets by pattern-matching 'convergence' to 'agreement', which is the misreading the item is built on. C and D swap the axis to language maintenance, a real creolistics variable that Text 2 never uses.

CS10-17.note: Text 2's first sentence names distance inland as the second thing isotope ratios record, and the rain-shadow argument follows from it. A (amount effect) and B (temperature) are genuine controls on oxygen isotopes in precipitation, so they are strong for a student with any isotope background; D (surface exposure) is the weak leg, a taphonomic process unrelated to rainfall ratios.

CS10-18.note: Text 2's point is a readership mismatch: emblem books belonged to a narrow clerical readership while the pictures hung in dining rooms and were priced by the square foot. A (language), B (engravings not mottoes) and C (closed libraries) are all alternative ways of severing buyer from book and each corresponds to a real misreading of 'books the paintings' buyers did not own'; only D matches the ownership argument actually made.
